title: Light
body: A day is three stretches of about five minutes: afternoon, night, then morning. The bright peak at the start of the afternoon is noon. Night holds the column dark between sunset and sunrise.

Light enters at the surface and is absorbed on the way down. The floor of the column keeps about a hundredth of the surface brightness. Ultraviolet falls off much faster, so it is gone a short way below the surface. The environment probe reads both.
Sunlight is what warms the upper water. The brightness of the day is the brightness of that warming.
